title: Social Media Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to harden your privacy on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X and other social platforms. Protect your data from tracking and harvesting.
intro: Social media platforms constantly change privacy settings and harvest your data for advertising. This comprehensive checklist helps you lock down your accounts across all major platforms to minimize data collection, prevent unauthorized access, and control who sees your information.

items.task: Enable two-factor authentication on all social media accounts
items.why: Prevents account takeovers even if your password is compromised. Essential protection against hackers and identity theft.
items.howTo: Go to Security settings in each platform. Enable 2FA using an authenticator app (preferred) or SMS. Save backup codes in a secure location. Test the setup before leaving settings.

items.task: Update to unique, strong passwords for each platform
items.why: Weak or reused passwords make you vulnerable to credential stuffing attacks and data breaches from other services.
items.howTo: Use a password manager to generate unique 12+ character passwords. Include uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Never reuse passwords across platforms.

items.task: Review and remove unrecognized active sessions
items.why: Old sessions from public computers or compromised devices can give unauthorized access to your accounts.
items.howTo: In Security settings, find 'Active Sessions' or 'Where You're Logged In'. Log out sessions from unknown devices or locations. Set up login alerts for new devices.

items.task: Verify and secure account recovery information
items.why: Outdated recovery emails or phone numbers can prevent account recovery or allow attackers to hijack your account.
items.howTo: Update recovery email to current secure address. Add backup phone number. Remove old or compromised contact methods. Test recovery process works.

items.task: Audit and remove unnecessary connected apps and services
items.why: Third-party apps often have broad permissions to access your data and can be security vulnerabilities or privacy risks.
items.howTo: Go to Apps/Applications in settings. Review each connected app's permissions. Remove apps you don't use. Limit permissions for remaining apps to minimum necessary.

items.task: Set profile and posts to private/friends only
items.why: Public profiles expose personal information to strangers, data scrapers, and can be used for social engineering attacks.
items.howTo: Change profile visibility to Friends/Followers only. Set future posts to private by default. Review who can see past posts and limit if needed. Hide friend/follower lists.

items.task: Prevent search engines from indexing your profile
items.why: Allows anyone to find your social media profiles through Google searches, exposing your information beyond the platform.
items.howTo: In Privacy settings, find 'Search' or 'Discoverability' options. Disable 'Allow search engines to link to your profile'. Turn off profile suggestions to strangers.

items.task: Disable contact syncing and phone/email lookup
items.why: Prevents platforms from suggesting your profile to people who have your contact info, and stops building shadow profiles from contacts.
items.howTo: Turn off 'Let others find you by phone/email'. Disable contact syncing. Delete previously uploaded contacts if option available. Opt out of friend suggestions based on contacts.

items.task: Require approval for tags and mentions
items.why: Prevents others from associating your name with content you haven't approved, protecting your reputation and privacy.
items.howTo: Enable tag/mention approval in Privacy settings. Set posts you're tagged in to require approval before appearing on your profile. Turn on notifications for tags.

items.task: Restrict who can send you direct messages
items.why: Reduces spam, harassment, and phishing attempts from strangers trying to contact you directly.
items.howTo: Set message permissions to Friends/Followers only. Enable message filtering for offensive content. Turn off read receipts to maintain privacy in conversations.

items.task: Turn off location sharing and check-ins
items.why: Location data reveals personal patterns, home/work addresses, and can be used for stalking or physical security threats.
items.howTo: Disable location services for social media apps in phone settings. Turn off location tagging in posts. Disable location history and nearby friends features.

items.task: Disable personalized ads and data sharing with advertisers
items.why: Reduces the amount of personal data collected for advertising and limits sharing with third-party advertisers and data brokers.
items.howTo: Go to Ad Preferences/Settings. Turn off personalized ads. Opt out of data sharing with partners. Clear existing ad interests and demographic categories. Disable off-platform activity tracking.

items.task: Download your data and review what's being collected
items.why: Understanding what data platforms have helps you make informed privacy decisions and identify concerning collection practices.
items.howTo: Use 'Download Your Data' tools in settings. Review collected information including messages, search history, and ad data. Delete unnecessary data where possible.

items.task: Disable facial recognition and auto-tagging features
items.why: Facial recognition creates biometric profiles that can be used for surveillance and makes you identifiable in photos you didn't consent to.
items.howTo: Turn off face recognition in Privacy settings. Disable auto-tagging suggestions. Delete existing face recognition data if deletion option is available.

items.task: Limit data sharing with Meta companies and partners
items.why: Prevents your social media data from being combined with data from other platforms and services for more comprehensive profiling.
items.howTo: In Privacy settings, find data sharing options. Disable sharing between Meta companies (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp). Opt out of sharing with external partners and advertisers.

items.task: Clear and disable off-platform activity tracking
items.why: Platforms track your browsing and purchases outside their sites to build detailed profiles for advertising and data monetization.
items.howTo: Find 'Off-Platform Activity' or similar in settings. Clear existing tracked activity. Turn off future activity tracking. Use Incognito Browser to prevent tracking cookies.

items.task: Configure TikTok's extensive data collection settings
items.why: TikTok collects more data than most platforms including device info, clipboard content, and biometric data for its algorithm.
items.howTo: Disable 'Suggest account to others', turn off 'Sync contacts', disable 'Personalized ads', turn off clipboard access in phone settings, and set account to private.

items.task: Adjust Instagram's less obvious privacy settings
items.why: Instagram has many privacy settings buried in different menus that aren't immediately obvious but significantly impact your privacy.
items.howTo: Turn off 'Similar account suggestions', disable 'Use contact info', turn off 'Share story to Facebook', disable 'Activity status', and turn off 'Shopping ads'.

items.task: Opt out of Facebook's detailed ad targeting categories
items.why: Facebook creates hundreds of interest categories based on your activity that can reveal sensitive information about health, finances, and beliefs.
items.howTo: Go to Ad Preferences > Categories used to reach you. Remove sensitive categories like health, financial, and lifestyle interests. Turn off partner categories.

items.task: Configure X (Twitter) discoverability and data settings
items.why: X shares data widely and has many discoverability features that can expose your account to unwanted attention and data collection.
items.howTo: Turn off 'Let others find you by email/phone', disable 'Personalized ads', turn off 'Track where you see Twitter content', and disable 'Share data with partners'.

items.task: Balance LinkedIn professional needs with privacy protection
items.why: LinkedIn requires some visibility for professional networking but has many data sharing features that go beyond necessary professional exposure.
items.howTo: Turn off 'Profile public visibility', disable 'Data for ads', turn off 'Profile data for research', disable 'Read receipts', and limit who can see your connections.

pro_tips: Use Incognito Browser when accessing social media to prevent cross-site tracking and maintain session isolation from your regular browsing.
Regularly audit your privacy settings as platforms frequently change defaults and add new data collection features without clear notification.
Consider using separate email addresses for social media accounts to isolate them from your primary email and reduce data correlation.
Review and clean up old posts, photos, and check-ins periodically - what seemed fine to share years ago might not align with your current privacy preferences.
Enable all available security notifications so you're immediately aware of login attempts, privacy setting changes, or suspicious account activity.
